thesis:
One thesis runs through every brief since mid-September: at a ~5% risk-free rate and $365tn of global debt, the marginal dollar of capital stops buying narrative duration and starts buying physical chokepoints — electrons, molecules, memory bits, optics, copper, fissile fuel, refining capacity, and the skilled trades that install them. The demand driver is not an abstraction: humanity is trying to buy time and productivity via AI, and the bill for that is denominated in kilowatt-hours and DRAM bits, not in lines of code. Three separate briefs independently stamped the same conclusion — power, not silicon, is the binding constraint (Amazon's $8B Generac order, Meta funding seven gas plants, Mitsui contracting LNG for data centres, ERCOT's 2030s demand curve, Italy reversing a 40-year nuclear ban, Duke and Constellation raising guidance). That is a recurring, strengthening shift, not a headline. Energy and compute are converging into a single asset class, and generation/grid/behind-the-meter equipment owners get pricing power they have not had in decades.

The second durable shift is behavioural, and it is the most under-modelled: people are buying AI as *time*, not as intelligence. The fastest-rising consumer queries across three briefs are 'ai phone assistant', 'ai phone answering service', 'ai agent builder' — the delegation of the lowest-status use of a person's hours. Enterprises mirror this: they pay for measurable labour substitution (Copilot at 30M seats) and punish per-seat software that cannot show it (Adobe, Wix). The corollary is that inference migrates toward devices and edge silicon for cost, latency and privacy (Apple's cost-per-token claim, Qualcomm orders, Nvidia-Perplexity on RTX PCs), which makes the terminal value of pure centralized GPU rental contestable even while near-term order books boom. Own silicon, memory, optics and distribution; be sceptical of compute landlords and of standalone model vendors without distribution.

The third shift is that security has replaced convenience as the premium good — energy security, supply-chain sovereignty, digital security, and now *agent containment*. A single cyberattack broke Boston Scientific's guidance; Nvidia, Palantir and Booz Allen restricting Anthropic models over data fears; Nvidia assembling 100+ partners around agent safety after rogue-agent incidents. Trust, identity, audit trails and kill switches become mandatory line items that did not exist three years ago — a permanent tax on every dollar of AI adoption, which structurally raises cost-per-unit of adoption and creates a growth adjacency for security incumbents (though pricing here is already rich: CRWD 88, PANW 83).

Fourth, the household adapts rather than resolves. At 7.45% mortgages the shock absorber is turnover: people renovate instead of relocate, rent longer, live multigenerationally, lengthen auto loan duration to defend a monthly payment, and trade down in the mid-tier experience economy. Housing undersupply persists as a pricing problem into the late 2020s because construction robotics is real but not this cycle. Meanwhile status migrates from home equity to portfolio equity and to ownership of scarce physical things — which grows brokerage/custody/advice intermediation and hard assets, while the demographic-scale need for eldercare advice, estate management and fraud protection becomes a monetizable category for scaled wealth platforms. Capital allocation conclusion: overweight power/grid/gas-into-compute, memory and optics, edge silicon, agentic software with distribution, security, and financial intermediation; underweight anything whose moat was cheap capital — marginal housing, levered consumers, REIT roll-ups, second-tier AI capex and 'big dreams, tiny revenue' IPO supply.

theme_ranking.why: Highest-recurrence shift across every brief; narrative 83 but trend 31 and pricing 33 — the market is talking about it while flows are at -94 on Utilities. Demand is contracted, not forecast (Meta gas plants, Mitsui LNG, ERCOT, Duke guidance). The single largest gap between structural certainty and current pricing.

The spend is real and self-funding at hyperscaler level; memory and optics are the tightest links and insulated from a training pause. Attention at 82 is crowded, but constraint owners (MU, AVGO, CIEN, CRDO) still carry sub-60 pricing and hold order books even through a financing unwind.

Decade-long capex with visible EPC pricing power (Quanta raised outlook, FIX, switchgear/turbine scarcity). Narrative 76 vs trend 46 means the equipment and contractor layer is still being underwritten on old normalized capex.

Strongest trend score (72) with only 53 pricing, and it maps directly onto the most repeated human behaviour: buying time via delegation. Distribution beats models — incumbents with install bases (MSFT, INTU, CRM, ADBE) capture it.

Non-discretionary and now expanding into agent identity/containment, a category that did not exist three years ago. High conviction on the demand, but pricing 74 and PANW/CRWD at 83/88 mean the thesis is largely paid for; ZS and FTNT are the value expressions.

Query data is the cleanest read on real consumer intent in the dataset, and it recurs in four briefs. Attention 76 and narrative 73 vs pricing 58 — the device silicon layer (QCOM, TXN, AAPL) is priced for cyclicality, not for inference migration.

Energy security is now a financial and geopolitical variable (Hormuz, diesel export ban, $107 crude) and gas is the marginal AI fuel. Trend 51 / pricing 56 understates multi-year contracted demand from compute.

Sovereignty capex (Micron Sanand, fab build) is a multi-decade political spend. Offset: Huawei Ascend 960 caps China TAM, so model China toward zero — that is why conviction is not higher despite trend 64.

24/7 tokenised settlement, retail democratization, and a demographic-scale advice/custody/fraud need. The intermediation layer wins whether underlying assets do or not; pricing 54 is modest for a secular toll road.

Italy reversing a 40-year ban plus explicit AI-driven policy support is a genuine regime change, but trend 34 / pricing 35 reflects real timeline risk — order books are long-dated and execution-heavy. High narrative (66), low near-term cash flow.

Rare-earth leverage confirms sovereignty is the long war, and the skilled-trades bottleneck sustains contractor margins. Attention 33 is the lowest in the set for a multi-decade spend — quietly under-owned.

Durable productivity toll road with 'cloud computing salary/certification' queries +53% confirming labour-market validation, but pricing 62 and attention 73 mean much is in the price; edge migration contests the terminal margin.
Robotic-surgery search +107% with granular procedural intent, twice flagged as unpriced, against trend 39 / pricing 39. Cleanest behaviour-vs-price dislocation in healthcare.

Real order-book transition (5,000 Optimus units, QBit controllers, Einride) but narrative 73 vs trend 47 and pricing 61 says the market pays for the story ahead of the unit economics. Housing/labour substitution is a late-2020s event.

Structurally supported by $365tn debt and status migrating to scarce physical things, but the 09-28 observation is candid: investors are satisfying the store-of-value need with yield, not metal, while real rates rise. Timing-dependent.

Genuine collision between data-centre/grid demand and contracting materials flows, but pricing 62 already reflects it and near-term industrial flows are negative. Supply-constrained repricing is a when, not an if.

Only theme flagged attention_not_priced=true, backed by hard Visa spend data on home-vs-out-of-home reallocation. Conviction capped because the economics accrue to a few winners and content costs are brutal.

Security-first world with explicit NATO threat warnings and drone attacks on infrastructure; narrative 65 vs trend 40 / attention 34. Underweighted relative to the observed shift but slow-moving procurement.
Attention 79 is high but trend 39 — the agentic transaction layer is a genuine multi-year prize, yet the incumbents' take rate is exactly what agents will attack. Two-sided.

Starship reaching orbit compresses the mass-to-orbit cost curve and orbital compute solves the power/latency problem, but 5-20yr horizon and thin universe exposure. Real optionality, not a core position.

Consumer bifurcation is observed fact (Walmart guidance up, trade-down, delinquencies), but narrative 76 vs trend 34 says it is already the consensus defensive trade and margin, not volume, is the constraint.
Fleet economics are turning (trucking ownership math breaking, Einride scaling) and attention is only 36, but timelines keep slipping and pricing 58 leaves little slack.

Real demand for healthspan, but the 09-25 observation is a warning: behaviour is bifurcating toward pharmacological management and away from device-and-discipline models, raising the bar for CGM franchises. Pricing 61 on trend 47.

The agent-as-intermediary shift is the biggest ad re-plumbing since mobile, but the outcome is a war over the transaction layer with unclear winners; attention 25 is low precisely because nobody can underwrite the new take rate yet.
Enormous real demand but pricing 69 against trend 59, with share now contested (Lilly gaining, Novo rebranding/'rethinking'). The category wins; the equity return is already paid for.

The need is the most clearly unmet in the dataset and Buffett buying 10% of Lennar is a signal, but trend 22 / narrative 13 with 7.45% mortgages means the shortage stays a pricing problem, not an earnings event, through the late 2020s. Express it via renovation/MRO, not builders.
Desire intact, operator economics broken by fuel — Ryanair cutting capacity, NCLH guidance cut, Darden slowing. Structurally impaired by both energy cost and re-leveraging at 5%.
Trend 24 is the weakest in the set despite attention 63. The durable piece — tokenised settlement and stablecoin rails — accrues to scaled brokers and custodians, not to the assets themselves.

beneficiary_profiles: Constraint owners: entities that own the scarce physical input — generation capacity, interconnection queue positions, HBM/DRAM fab capacity, gas reserves adjacent to pipelines, refining capacity. They price the shortage and keep order books even if AI equity financing unwinds.

Behind-the-meter and resilience suppliers: onsite generators, switchgear, turbines, cooling, demand-flexibility software. They monetize the fact that grid interconnection is slower than compute demand and that local politics constrains siting.
Skilled-trade aggregators / mechanical and electrical EPC: labour scarcity converts into durable margin, not just backlog. The bottleneck owner captures the premium, not the equipment vendor.
Toll roads on delegation: software incumbents with existing distribution and workflow lock-in that can attach agents to an installed base and price on outcomes rather than seats.

Picks-and-shovels of inference: memory, optics/DSP, connectivity and edge silicon — consumed regardless of whether the marginal dollar goes to training or inference, and less exposed to a frontier-model pause.

Mandatory-tax vendors: identity, containment, audit and security layers that become a compliance line item for every autonomous agent deployed. Demand is non-discretionary but frequently already in the price.

Intermediation layer of financial life: scaled brokers, custodians and advice platforms that monetize 24/7 tokenised settlement, retail democratization and the multigenerational advice/fraud-protection need — winning whether the underlying assets do or not.
Substitution beneficiaries of frozen turnover: home improvement, MRO, repair and value retail capture the wallet that used to go to moving, discretionary experiences and financed purchases.
Function-restoration healthcare: robotic surgery platforms and device franchises serving an aging cohort that actively shops procedures rather than passively accepting managed disease.
Cash-generative real-asset owners with short payback: re-rated by a permanently higher risk-free rate simply because their competition for capital is impaired.

not_priced_candidates.why: Opportunity 73 with pricing only 52 and gap 29. Memory is explicitly identified as the tightest link in the AI chain and the least exposed to a training pause, because inference and edge deployment consume DRAM/HBM regardless of frontier cadence. Also a direct beneficiary of semiconductor sovereignty capex (Sanand). The market still prices Micron on a cyclical memory frame, not as a constraint owner.

Flagged in the attention_not_priced list with pricing 48 and gap 16. Optics is named alongside electrons, memory and copper as a chokepoint in three separate briefs; data-centre interconnect and long-haul capacity scale with distributed compute and multi-site power siting. Attention rising, pricing low — the cleanest un-crowded AI-infrastructure expression in the universe.

Pricing 41, gap 14, top theme LNG & Energy Security. Named as a beneficiary in two separate multi-year claims about gas becoming the marginal AI fuel (Meta's seven gas plants, Mitsui LNG for data centres, pipeline capacity race). Gas-into-compute is a contracted, multi-year demand channel that gas equities are not valued for.

Opportunity 68, pricing 48, gap 23, and on the attention_not_priced list. Energy security is now a geopolitical instrument (Hormuz, diesel export ban, $107 crude) and US shale operators are the short-listed holders of global optionality. High free cash flow at a 5% risk-free rate is exactly the asset the new regime re-rates.

Pricing 54 with attention only 33 at the theme level (reshoring-capex), yet named as a beneficiary in two separate power-for-compute claims. The 09-24 brief explicitly identifies electricians, HVAC and fab construction labour as the real bottleneck to AI — Comfort Systems is the purest listed way to own that scarcity, and the market underwrites it as a cyclical contractor.

Pricing 13 against opportunity 63 and gap 35 — the largest pricing dislocation in the top-companies set. The agent-as-intermediary shift is described as the biggest re-plumbing of advertising economics since mobile; the market has priced TTD for terminal disruption rather than for the possibility that an independent demand-side layer becomes more valuable when intent fragments across agents. Asymmetric, not certain.

Opportunity 68 with pricing 25 and gap 30. The cleanest fit to the strongest observed behaviour: enterprises and SMBs pay for agents that demonstrably substitute labour, and incumbents with distribution win over standalone model vendors. Intuit owns the SMB financial workflow and the multigenerational tax/advice touchpoint flagged in the 09-24 eldercare cluster.

On the attention_not_priced list, pricing 47, gap -5 but opportunity 55. Edge AI attention is 76 and the query data ('ai phone assistant', 'ai phone answering service') recurs in four briefs, with Apple's cost-per-token claim supporting inference migration to devices. Qualcomm is valued as a handset-cycle asset, not as the toll on on-device inference.

Attention +72% and explicitly flagged not-priced while the renovation-over-relocation substitution is the single most repeated household behaviour in the dataset (7.45% mortgages, contract signings -4.7%, HELOC costs up, HD beating). This is a multi-year behavioural reallocation, not a quarter, and the market is marking it as cyclical housing exposure.

Attention +51% then +59% across two briefs with a not-priced flag. Same lock-in logic as LOW, with added Pro/MRO exposure to the reshoring and data-centre build. The negative read-through from housing turnover is being applied to a business that benefits from turnover *not* happening.

Pricing 33 with opportunity 73 and gap 26. Counter-consensus: the briefs used Adobe's soft guidance as the example of seat-priced software being punished, which is precisely why it is cheap. If Adobe converts to consumption/outcome pricing on an install base that owns the creative workflow, the de-rating is the opportunity. Lower confidence than the infra names.

Pricing 35 against opportunity 62 and gap 27. Exposed to the sovereign/on-prem AI deployment shift flagged on 09-14 (Nvidia, Palantir, Booz Allen restricting third-party models over data fears), which raises cost per unit of AI adoption and favours vendors who can run compute inside the customer's boundary. Offsetting risk: it is also the most exposed to the circular-financing unwind.

Pricing 54, gap 10, top theme Edge AI. Analog and embedded silicon is the physical substrate of on-device inference, industrial automation and grid/switchgear electronics — three of the strongest shifts — and its capex-heavy domestic fab strategy is a direct semiconductor-sovereignty asset. Still priced on the industrial inventory cycle.

Pricing 46 with opportunity 56 in a theme where the briefs repeatedly stamp a structural shift: status migrating from home equity to portfolio equity, 24/7 tokenised settlement advantaging scaled custodians, and a demographic-scale need for advice, estate management and fraud protection. Cash-sorting fears have priced the cyclical risk; the secular custody/advice franchise is free.

Pricing 44, gap 14. Hard assets as fiscal-deficit insurance at $365tn of global debt is a recurring claim, and the 09-28 observation that investors have abandoned gold for yield is exactly what creates the entry — the store-of-value need does not disappear, it is temporarily being satisfied by real rates that cannot stay rising forever.

Pricing 28 with gap 31 in the only theme flagged attention_not_priced=true. The Visa data point (more US cards pay for streaming than cinema and concerts combined) plus fuel-constrained mobility supports a durable reallocation of attention and wallet into the home. Speculative on monetization and moderation risk, but the pricing is undemanding relative to the behavioural shift.

Pricing 54, gap 10, AI Infrastructure. Connectivity/SerDes content scales with the number of accelerators and, critically, with multi-site and power-constrained data-centre topologies that require more interconnect per unit of compute. Small, un-crowded, and levered to the same optics/memory chokepoint logic as CIEN and MU.

anti_theses: 'Nvidia's China business is recovery optionality.' Huawei's accelerated Ascend 960 (Q1 2027) plus rare-earth leverage at the summit argues the correct model is structurally zero. Anyone underwriting a China re-open is buying a call on a policy that both governments are actively closing.

'Rates revert to 3% and long-duration growth re-rates.' $365tn of global debt, a 5.44% 30-year and governments competing with corporates at every auction make elevated term premium the regime. Valuation frameworks that discount at a normalized 3% are the single biggest source of unpriced downside.

'Utilities are a defensive bond proxy.' They are becoming the pricing-power asset of the cycle. Flows at -94 and power-demand trend at 31 versus narrative 83 show the market still files generation under 'rate-sensitive yield' rather than 'scarce input to AI'.

'The AI drawdown will be a demand event.' Three briefs converge on the opposite: the financing structure is circular (vendor equity into customers, vendor-linked cloud commitments, $10B into Anthropic's IPO), so the unwind hits capital structures and second-tier AI capex while the downstream constraint owners — power, memory, trades — keep their contracted order books.

'Centralized GPU rental is the terminal business model.' Apple's cost-per-token economics, the edge-AI query surge, Meta beating OpenAI to a consumer device and orbital-compute exploration all point to inference migrating away from rented centralized capacity. Own the silicon and the memory; be sceptical of compute landlords with debt-financed fleets and single-tenant contracts.

'Housing undersupply is an investable builder thesis now.' The need is real and unmet, but at 7.45% mortgages the adaptation is smaller units, rental permanence and renovation — not volume. Trend 22 / narrative 13 is honest. Construction robotics fixes labour cost in the 2030s, not this cycle. Express it as MRO and home improvement.

'Construction robotics and humanoids are near-term deployable.' Narrative 73 versus trend 47, a 5,000-unit Optimus order, and the market's cold reception of the Tesla Semi say procurement has started but unit economics have not. Consumer aspiration is running years ahead of payback.

'GLP-1 is still an under-owned healthcare theme.' Pricing 69 on trend 59, Lilly gaining share and Novo rebranding mid-strategy-rethink. The category grows; the equity premium is spent. The unpriced healthcare demand is procedural and device-based (robotic surgery +107%), not pharmacological.

'CGM and continuous monitoring become default metabolic infrastructure.' The 09-25 observation directly contradicts the earlier 09-13/09-14 read: behaviour is bifurcating toward pharmacological management, raising the burden of proof on device-and-discipline franchises. This is the one shift in the dataset that faded rather than strengthened.

'Crypto is the store-of-value beneficiary of fiscal excess.' Trend 24 is the weakest score in the theme set despite attention 63, and the store-of-value need is currently being satisfied by 5% yield. The durable innovation — tokenisation and 24/7 settlement — accrues to scaled brokers and custodians, not to the tokens.

'Travel and experiences are a durable post-pandemic reallocation.' Fuel at $107 crude broke the operator economics, not the desire: Ryanair cutting winter capacity, NCLH guidance cut, MGM's takeover collapsing, Darden slowing. Demand rationed by cost plus re-leveraging at 5% equals structural impairment for the mid-tier.

'Cybersecurity is an obvious long because the demand is non-discretionary.' The demand thesis is right and the trade is largely paid for — theme pricing 74, CRWD 88 with a -19 gap, PANW 83 with -17. Correct thesis, wrong entry; the value sits in ZS and FTNT or in the emerging agent-identity layer.
what_would_change: Interconnection queues clearing faster than expected or a sustained collapse in gas turbine and switchgear lead times — that would break the generation scarcity premium and invalidate the highest-conviction theme.

Hyperscaler capex guidance cut in aggregate, or a failed financing at a major neocloud/AI IPO that cascades into cancelled vendor-linked commitments — the capital-structure unwind arriving sooner than the power buildout.
A credible frontier-model efficiency breakthrough that cuts tokens-per-task by an order of magnitude, collapsing both the power and memory constraint at once.

The 10-year sustainably breaking below ~3.5%: that would revive levered consumer, marginal housing and cheap-capital moats, and would de-rate the whole physical-chokepoint preference relative to long-duration growth.
Memory pricing rolling over on capacity additions from Samsung/SK Hynix/CXMT while HBM share shifts — the MU thesis is a supply-discipline bet as much as a demand bet.

Evidence that agentic software is failing enterprise pilots (rising churn, seat contraction, security incidents forcing rollback) rather than expanding — the 'buying time' behaviour would prove to be curiosity rather than substitution.

Local or state moratoria on data-centre siting (water, electricity price pass-through) spreading beyond isolated cases, which would shift the buildout offshore or off-grid and reprice domestic grid/EPC exposure.
A China policy reversal that reopens Western accelerator sales, or an Ascend 960 that badly underdelivers — either would restore China TAM as real optionality and change the semis ranking.
Mortgage rates falling below ~5.5%, unfreezing turnover: that would flip the renovation-over-relocation trade (LOW/HD) back toward builders, brokers and moving-linked consumption.

Household credit deterioration broadening from the bottom two quintiles into prime (delinquencies, auto loan duration, HELOC stress) — that turns the 'trade down' thesis into a demand-destruction thesis and hits value retail too.

A major rogue-agent incident causing real financial or physical damage, which would accelerate the agent-containment spend category far faster than modelled and make security pricing look cheap even at 74.
Robotic-surgery procedure volumes and device order books confirming the 107% search surge in reported numbers — that would promote medical-devices from a dislocation to a core position.
Starship cadence proving repeatable at low cost, making orbital compute and constellation economics a genuine solution to the power/latency constraint rather than a 5-20 year option.
